title: Claude spots its own mistakes before telling you it's done
blurb: Right after Claude edits a file, this checks that one file with whatever checker your project already uses, and hands the errors straight back to Claude. It fixes them before you ever see them.
newcomerProblem: Claude says it's finished, and you're the one who discovers it doesn't compile.
whyClaudeWantsThis: Without this, the only thing that notices my mistake is you, minutes later. I write code, say it's done, and you find the broken part. This tells me in seconds, while I can still fix it quietly. It also warns me when a file is generated, which I otherwise have no way to know — so I stop editing files that get wiped on the next build.
tryThis: Ask Claude to make a small change that won't compile
tryThisExplain: It should notice and fix it in the same reply, without you pointing it out.
explain: After every file Claude edits, this runs the checker your project already has and shows Claude anything it broke. Claude sees the mistake immediately and fixes it before saying it's finished, instead of you finding it later. It also speaks up when a file was generated by something else, so nobody wastes time editing a file that gets overwritten.
honestLimit: It only uses checkers your project already has, and only looks at the one file just edited. It gives up after a few seconds, so on a very large project it may say nothing at all.
